$comment: Hypotheses v2 (#685), frozen before the v2 tasks, answer keys and any live run. v1 (../hypotheses.json) stays frozen and unchanged. Do not tune after seeing results: a change needs its own commit and a new baseline.
comparison: graph arm versus native arm, same client, model, effort and prompt prefix

definitions.taskScore: Mean of the field scores of one answer, in [0, 1]. A scalar field scores 1 on exact match, else 0. A list field scores the F1 of its precision and recall against the key. Malformed or missing JSON scores 0.
definitions.correctness: Sum over the class tasks of the task score, each task averaged over its completed runs.
definitions.recall: Sum over the class tasks of the recall of the list fields, each task averaged over its completed runs.
definitions.correctnessGain: (graph correctness - native correctness) / number of class tasks: the mean score gain per task.
definitions.toolCalls: Sum over the class tasks of the tool calls, each task averaged over its completed runs.
definitions.providerTokens: Sum over the class tasks of non-cached input tokens, cache-write tokens and output tokens reported by the client, each task averaged over its completed runs. Cache reads are input, never savings. cl100k_base counts and JSON/TOON sizes are not provider tokens.
definitions.reduction: (native - graph) / native for a metric; undefined when native is 0 or the metric is unavailable in either arm.

transitive-impact.hypothesis: Callers or dependents at depth >= 2, one task per corpus language (TypeScript, Python, Vue). Correctness >= native and recall >= native; and either a correctness gain >= 0.25 per task, or >= 20 % fewer tool calls or provider tokens.

call-path.hypothesis: The methods on a call chain of 4 or more hops. Correctness >= native and recall >= native; and either a correctness gain >= 0.25 per task, or >= 20 % fewer tool calls or provider tokens.

global-structure.hypothesis: The files on an import cycle through one file. Correctness >= native and recall >= native; and either a correctness gain >= 0.25 per task, or >= 20 % fewer tool calls or provider tokens.

known-file.hypothesis: Control, v1 task on this repository: the prompt gives the file. Same correctness, at most +1 tool call and at most +25 % provider tokens. More than that confirms that forced retrieval is overhead.

greppable-name.hypothesis: Control, v1 task on this repository: the prompt names the symbol and one search lists its callers. Native should win or tie: same correctness, at most +1 tool call and at most +25 % provider tokens.

verdicts.refuted: Graph correctness (or, for classes with minRecallDelta, recall) lower than native, even with an efficiency gain; or a control above one of its limits.
verdicts.confirmed: Every condition of the hypothesis holds.
verdicts.notConfirmed: Neither refuted nor confirmed: no correctness gain and an efficiency difference within the threshold, a metric unavailable in either arm, a control with higher graph correctness, or a task without a completed run in either arm.
verdicts.sampleSize: Each verdict states its task and run counts and is never presented as statistically significant.
verdicts.changeFromV1: minCorrectnessGain is new: on tasks one search cannot answer, a better answer at a higher cost is the value under test, so a correctness gain also confirms. Every other rule is the v1 rule.

limits: Corpora: three public open-source projects at pinned commits, plus this repository for the two controls. The models may know these projects from training, so the questions target details of the pinned commits; results do not generalize to large private repositories.
One repetition by default and 1-3 tasks per class: verdicts detect large differences only and are never statistically significant.
Clients differ in automation and observable metrics; the report does not imply feature parity.
Notional cost is computed by the client, never actual spend. cl100k_base and JSON/TOON sizes are retrieval estimates, not provider usage.
